edema.what: Edema: swollen brain tissue around the tumor (bright on FLAIR / T2).
edema.effect: It adds pressure on nearby brain (mass effect) and often causes headaches; steroids can reduce it.

enhancing_tumor.what: Active tumor: the growing rim where contrast leaks through damaged blood vessels.
enhancing_tumor.effect: This is the part doctors measure to judge whether treatment is working (RANO).

necrotic_core.what: Necrotic core: dead tumor tissue in the middle.
necrotic_core.effect: A sign of fast growth, typical of high-grade gliomas; it does not shrink much with treatment.

tumor.what: Tumor (the model does not separate its parts here).
tumor.effect: Its size and position decide which nearby functions could be affected.

lesion.effect: Its shape, edges and orientation help tell benign from malignant; a biopsy confirms.

nodule.what: Lung nodule: a small round spot in the lung.
nodule.effect: Most are benign; its size and growth on follow-up CT decide what happens next (Lung-RADS).

possible_extent.what: Possible extent: how deep the tumor could reach.
possible_extent.effect: One image cannot show depth; 9 out of 10 real tumors are shallower than this shell.

classification.label: tumor
classification.display: Lung nodule found (it does not tell benign from malignant)

location.image_position: upper left part of the image

lung_rads.typical_management: Chest CT, PET/CT and/or tissue sampling, per the care team
lung_rads.assumptions: Solid nodule on a baseline screening CT. The real category also depends on nodule type, growth compared with earlier scans and other features that this tool does not assess.
